title: stargazer-midshift-field-notes
body:
Purpose
Quick mid-shift scratchpad for handoff — things I observed, temporary mitigations I applied, open follow-ups. Treat as ephemeral notes; most of this should be migrated into the formal oncall runbook if it proves stable.

Summary at a glance
- Window: 02/10 22:00 - 02/11 02:00 PST
- Primary issue: intermittent routing spikes to hosted-model-quant-a causing tail latency >1200ms for short batches (p99).
- Impact: degraded interactive latencies for <50-token chat flows on prod-us-west (2.3% of requests hit SLO breach during 22:15–23:05).
- Temporary mitigation: enabled manual routing fallback to hosted-model-quant-b (lower capacity but better short-seq tail) and applied a KV-cache warmup on the affected shard.

What I observed (timeline notes)
- 22:07: Alert INF-agg: p99_gen_latency_prod_us_west crossed 1200ms (threshold).
- 22:09: Spike correlated with a burst from client X (spike pattern: many concurrent short sequences). Looked like an N+1 test run from their env (ticket INF-8742 includes more).
- 22:12: Autoscaler started scaling up pool quant-a but new instances came up with cold KV caches -> initial requests slower -> cascade.
- 22:18: Manual route policy change: route policy for 'chat-short' class -> prefer quant-b (lower mem footprint) enacted. Latency dropped toward baseline by 22:24.
- 22:30: Noticed error rate for quant-b rising from 0.02% -> 0.5% (OOM-like 509s). Rolled back some old kernel flags on quant-b (temp fix) at 22:38.
- 23:04: Situation stable. Left sticky notes for oncoming.

Quick commands I ran (LOGS + PROD)
- kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=quant-a -o wide  # check pod ages/ready
- curl -sS "https://metrics-api/prod/latency?p99&range=5m" | jq .  # sanity pull of p99 trend
- rwctl routing set-priority --route chat-short --prefer hosted-model-quant-b --reason "temp midshift fallback"
- rwctl cache warmup --shard s-7 --model hosted-model-quant-a --prefix  "clientX/" --batch 50
- kubectl logs -n inference pod/<pod-name> --tail=500 | grep -i "cuda oom"  # quick grep
Note: rwctl is the short alias for our routing control CLI (local wrapper around the control plane).

Temporary mitigations applied (do not delete)
- Routing: chat-short traffic routed to hosted-model-quant-b for prod-us-west (policy ID: route-20260210-midshift1).
- Cache warmup: invoked for quant-a shard s-7. Warmup used 2k prefixes (clientX top paths) to reduce cold-start latency.
- Kernel flags: reverted experimental kernel-opt XLA-vec-2 on quant-b nodes to stop transient 509s (flag revert id: revert-20260210-kf1).

Why this happened (hypothesis)
- Workload mismatch: sudden burst of many short sequences defeats batch accumulation heuristics -> autoscaler and runtime spawn new nodes that start cold (KV cache miss), causing initial requests to be slow and increasing observed p99.
- Quant-a has a larger batch/throughput orientation; its warmup penalty is higher for many tiny requests.
- Quant-b handles short sequences better but is more memory-constrained; a kernel-opt change earlier this week made it marginally less stable under bursty concurrency.

Short-term actions for next shift (explicit handoff)
- If p99 > 1000ms again: 1) confirm clientX burst ID in INF-8742, 2) immediately re-run "rwctl routing set-priority --route chat-short --prefer hosted-model-quant-b --reason \"p99 fallback\"" 3) trigger cache warmup on previous shard(s).
- If quant-b 5xxs > 0.5%: rollback the kernel flags (revert-20260210-kf1) and open infra CR to audit kernel changes (ticket INF-8790).
- If autoscaler keeps oscillating: temporarily disable autoscale-burst for quant-a pool and open an engineering follow-up to tune scale-up cooldowns (sx: recommend 90s).

Longer-term follow-ups (create tickets / owners)
- INF-8791: Improve warmup automation: when new node boots, kick KV-prefetch for hot prefixes from recent 1h traces. (Owner: Priya)
- INF-8792: Add per-route short-seq routing policy that prefers quant-b for seq_len < 64 without full pool migration (Owner: Omar)
- INF-8793: Root cause kernel-opt regression on quant-b and add pre-release canary for kernel flags (Owner: infra-release)
- INF-8794: Add canary synthetic traffic for common short sequences from clientX to detect cold-start pain before user impact (Owner: SRE)

Escalation contacts (if things get worse)
- Onsite infra lead: Miguel Torres (pager: SRE-Lead), Slack: @miguel.t
- Runtime perf: Dr. Alice Monroe (pager: PERF-ENG), Slack: @alice.m
- Product contact (clientX): Simon Lee (AM) — if customer complains escalate via sales-desk line.

Open questions / notes to document later
- Do we have a per-pool warmup budget? Need to capture exact costs (GPU/compute) for 2k prefix warmup. (Cost owner: infra-costing)
- Investigate whether kernel-opt XLA-vec-2 provides net gain for long-seq throughput enough to warrant short-seq instability. If yes, need targeted flow-level flags.

Checklist for next handoff (short)
- [ ] Confirm route-policy state: rwctl routing list --route chat-short
- [ ] Check p99 timeline graph for last 2h (metrics dashboard link below)
- [ ] Verify any recent infra changes in the last 6h (release-engineering Slack #releases)
- [ ] Leave links to any created tickets in the ticket tracker and add them to oncall shift notes page

Useful links and dashboards
- p99 dashboard (prod-us-west chat-short): https://dashboards.internal.redwood/p99-chat-short-us-west
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8742
- Routing control docs: confluence:redwood/routing-control
- Warmup tool README: https://git.internal.redwood/tools/kv-warmup/README.md

Personal notes (why I did what I did)
- I prioritized reducing user-visible p99 first even if it meant moving some traffic to less efficient models — customer experience > marginal cost increase during short incident window.
- I left a couple of marker tickets instead of making broad infra changes mid-shift (didn't have the time/eyes to validate kernel impacts).

Handing off to: Omar Nguyen (next oncall)
- Omar: main things to check first: routing policy state, p99 trend, quant-b 5xx rate. If all green, revert the manual routing change in 3 hours to test stability.

Final: logging the actions I took to the shift notes thread: slack thread #sre-oncall -> message id saved in INF-8742.

Raw scratch area (commands / quick grep results pasted here for visibility)
- pod ages: quant-a pods (s-7) -> [12m, 9m, 8m] (evidence of recent scale-up)
- tail logs snippet: "[22:10:03] WARN kv_cache: miss for prefix clientX/flow/abc -> initiating warmup"
- curl latency snapshot: {"p50":78,"p90":230,"p99":1214} at 22:10

-- end of midshift notes --
